title: Handling Charge on a Keyturn Trip Booking Mileage Top-Up, by the Source of the Latest Odometer Reading
content:
Where a Keyturn Trip Booking has been running for at least 28 days, that is four weeks, the handling charge on a top-up of included miles is set by where the latest odometer reading booked against the reservation came from.

1. Where the latest odometer reading booked against the reservation came from the marketplace's telematics and the trip has run for at least 28 days, no handling charge is made, which is to say the charge is 0.00 USD.
2. Where the latest odometer reading booked against the reservation was reported by the host or by the guest and the trip has run for at least 28 days, the handling charge is 12.00 USD.
3. In every other case the handling charge is the standard one.

### What counts as a reading, and how the days are counted

The odometer readings counted here are the records the reservation's mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics, the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked.

The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The combinations

| Source of the latest odometer reading | Days the trip has run | Handling charge |
|---|---|---|
| The marketplace's telematics | 28 or more | 0.00 USD |
| Reported by the host | 28 or more | 12.00 USD |
| Reported by the guest | 28 or more | 12.00 USD |
| Any | Fewer than 28 | The standard one |

Only the latest reading booked against the reservation is read; earlier readings and their sources make no difference. A host report and a guest report are treated alike, at 12.00 USD. Twenty-eight days is reached rather than passed, so a trip running exactly 28 days sits in the first or second row.

*Hypothetical.* A trip running 52 days whose latest odometer reading came from the marketplace's telematics carries no handling charge. The same trip, where the latest reading was one the guest reported, carries a handling charge of 12.00 USD. A trip running 9 days carries the standard handling charge whichever source its latest reading came from.
